sections.name: Vengefly
sections.card:
Summary: A flying enemy that turns up in many areas, from King's Pass and the Forgotten Crossroads to Greenpath and the City of Tears. It hovers in a small area, squawks, then flies at you, and it is among the earliest and simplest enemies in the game.
Weak points: It flies straight at you once you are in range, so you can wait where you stand and hit it as it arrives, or jump and strike downward onto it.
Tips: Because it keeps coming at you, you can stay in one spot and keep swinging until it dies. Unlike most enemies, it comes back after you leave the room and return.

sections.name: Aspid Hunter
sections.card:
Summary: A hovering spitter that drifts around until you come close, then fires blobs of corrosive liquid from a distance. It usually hunts in packs, and you meet it in the Forgotten Crossroads and at the western end of the Ancient Basin's tram tunnel.
Weak points: Right when it has finished spitting you get a short opening, so close in and hit it at once.
Tips: You can hear the whirring of its wings from far off, so you know one is near before you see it. A tougher version, the Primal Aspid, lives in Kingdom's Edge. Like a few other enemies, it comes back when you leave the room and return.

sections.name: Husk Guard
sections.card:
Summary: A club-wielding husk that stands at its post until you come near, then rushes in. Only two exist in the Forgotten Crossroads: one just east of where you fight the False Knight, and one above the northern entrance to Crystal Peak.
Weak points: Once its club has come down it is open to your nail. After its shockwave, jump the wave toward it and land one or two hits. You can also hit it once and slip out of range before the club falls, but the gap is small, and the Mothwing Cloak makes it easier.
Tips: Its overhead club slam costs two masks, and its backward hop sends a shockwave left and right along the ground that widens and speeds up as it goes. The guard met before the False Knight can be hit safely from the right-hand platform. Each drops 45 Geo, a high amount this early, and both are near the Stag Station, so they are a quick source of Geo; fight the one by the False Knight's arena early, because it cannot be fought once the Crossroads changes.

sections.name: Heavy Sentry
sections.card:
Summary: A walking corpse that wields a greatnail and guards the City of Tears, where a few are found; two more stand in the east of the Royal Waterways.
Weak points: Hit it when it charges: jump over it and strike down, or cast Vengeful Spirit or Shade Soul, because it cannot dodge them then. You can also hit it just after its ordinary overhead swing.
Tips: It has three attacks: an overhead swing, a charge with the nail held out in front, and a hop. The hop is its answer to a jump over it: it rises, hurts on contact and swings again as it lands, so time your jump for its charge.
Looks like: A walking corpse that carries a greatnail.

sections.name: Mantis Youth
sections.card:
Summary: A young member of the mantis tribe that clings to a wall or the ceiling to ambush you. You find it only inside Mantis Village and by its entrance.
Tips: Once it engages, it hovers just beyond nail reach, winds up and lunges; the lunge covers little ground and is simple to avoid, but it floats out of range at once to wind up again. After the Mantis Lords fall, mantises stop attacking you but still hit back if you strike them. Like a few other enemies, it returns when you leave the room and come back.

sections.name: Soul Twister
sections.card:
Summary: A scholar of the Soul Sanctum that teleports around and throws homing soul orbs at you. You meet it east of the Soul Master's arena, and in later waves of the Trial of the Fool.
Weak points: It cannot teleport straight after it fires, so dodge the orb by jumping or dashing and then rush in. Nail Arts, Great Slash for one, kill it fast, Dash Slash closes the gap, and Vengeful Spirit or Shade Soul reaches it at range because it does not teleport away from them on purpose.
Tips: It teleports often, so you cannot corner it; small rooms and halls give it fewer angles, which makes its orbs easier to read and gives you more openings. Running is hard, but it will not follow you through a screen transition into another room.

sections.name: Crystal Hunter
sections.card:
Summary: A hovering creature found only in Crystal Peak that usually stays out of nail reach and shoots crystals at you.
Weak points: It fires with a short delay, so it tends to miss unless you stand right under it; jump up and slash it while it prepares the next shot.
Tips: Its shot bursts into a clump of crystals on hitting a surface. The clump fades after a short while, a nail hit breaks it easily, and you can bounce off it with your nail. A nail strike can also deflect the shot itself, though the shot still passes through enemies.
Looks like: A hovering creature with crystal growths on its body.

sections.name: Great Hopper
sections.card:
Summary: The grown-up form of the Hopper, a big leaper that hops without stopping and shakes the ground each time it lands. You find it in the southeast of Kingdom's Edge and in the Trial of the Conqueror, and hitting the dummy at Oro's backyard sets two on you.
Weak points: Stand still and step a little to the side to dodge its jumps, and you can strike it after each landing and take no damage. Howling Wraiths or Abyss Shriek can damage it while it is in the air.
Tips: Touching it hurts. Unlike a normal Hopper, it turns around to chase you.
Looks like: A large hopping creature, the full-grown version of the ordinary Hopper.

sections.name: Baldur
sections.card:
Summary: A crawling creature that rolls into a ball and launches itself at you. It lives in the Ancestral Mound, the Crystallised Mound and the Howling Cliffs, and a stronger kind, the Sharp Baldur, fights in the Colosseum of Fools.
Weak points: When it nears you, jump over it and strike down onto it. The Quick Slash or Heavy Blow charm lets you keep knocking it back before it touches you.
Tips: While curled up it rebounds from walls and from other Baldurs, then uncurls after a short time and turns to face you again.
Looks like: A crawling creature with orange eyes that curls up into a ball.

sections.name: Gruz Mother
sections.card:
Summary: A sleeping boss in a small arena in the Forgotten Crossroads, standing across the direct path to a deserted village at the bottom. She wakes when you hit her, and two more are fought together in the Trial of the Warrior.
Weak points: She has low health, so the simplest kill is with Vengeful Spirit: six casts or 18 hits with the Old Nail are enough.
Tips: Her repeated slams between floor and ceiling are fast and need good timing, which the Mothwing Cloak makes easier. When she dies in the Crossroads she bursts into 7 or 8 Gruzzers that you must also kill before you can leave. In the Trial of the Warrior two come at once: kill one as fast as you can, and Howling Wraiths or Abyss Shriek works best.
